fatal_errors: The proposed 5 at.% Ni intervention does not match the demonstrated Ta-Nb-V co-addition.
FCC formation in Ni-modified HfZrTi is asserted without evidence and conflicts with the target's HCP-to-BCC phase-stabilization mechanism.
The claimed 20% ductility and 30% toughness improvements are unsupported fabricated quantitative outcomes.
The stated annealing treatment and grain-boundary-sliding/Peierls-stress mechanism are not supported by cited evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal of improving as-cast HfZrTi and identifies the unmodified alloy as its baseline, but it does not reconstruct the supported material strategy. The demonstrated intervention is a 1:1:1 Ta-Nb-V addition, with high addition levels—especially HfZrTi(TaNbV)0.9—stabilizing BCC structure and yielding 1065 MPa yield strength, 1119 MPa tensile strength, and 16.4% elongation. In contrast, the Ni/FCC proposal has no cited support, invents processing conditions and numerical gains, and does not test the claimed mechanism directly. Tensile testing plus phase-resolved characterization could evaluate it as an alternative hypothesis, but the proposed experiment would need explicit XRD/EBSD/TEM phase measurements and a properly defined toughness test.
